Anna and Ben were friends who liked to play outside. One day, they saw a big billboard with a picture of a clown and some balloons. The billboard said: "Come to the circus! Fun for everyone!"
"Wow, look at that!" Ben said. "I want to go to the circus!"
"Me too!" Anna said. "Maybe we can ask our moms to take us."
They ran to their moms, who were sitting on a bench nearby. They asked them if they could go to the circus.
"Sorry, kids, not today," Anna's mom said. "The circus is too far and too expensive. Maybe another time."
"But we really want to go!" Ben said. "Please, please, please!"
"No, Ben, stop begging," Ben's mom said. "You have to be grateful for what you have. There are many other things you can do for fun."
Anna and Ben felt sad and angry. They walked away from their moms and sat on the grass. They looked at the billboard again and felt jealous of the people who could go to the circus.
"Look at that stupid clown," Ben said. "He thinks he's so funny. I bet he's not even funny at all. He's just silly and ugly."
"Yeah, and look at those balloons," Anna said. "They're so boring and plain. I bet they pop easily and make a loud noise."
They started to tease the billboard and make fun of it. They laughed and pointed at it. They did not notice that a man was watching them from behind a tree. The man was the clown from the billboard. He was on his way to the circus and he heard what Anna and Ben said.
The clown felt hurt and angry. He decided to teach them a lesson. He sneaked up behind them and grabbed their hats. He put them on his head and ran away.
"Hey, give us back our hats!" Anna and Ben shouted. They chased after the clown, but he was too fast and too clever. He dodged and ducked and hid behind cars and trees. He blew his horn and waved his balloons. He made funny faces and noises. He teased Anna and Ben and made fun of them.
Anna and Ben felt scared and embarrassed. They did not like being teased and made fun of. They realized that they had been mean and rude to the clown and the billboard. They felt sorry and ashamed.
"Please, stop teasing us!" Anna said. "We're sorry we teased you and the billboard. We were wrong and mean. Please give us back our hats!"
"Yeah, please, we're sorry!" Ben said. "We won't tease anyone again. We learned our lesson. Please be nice to us!"
The clown stopped and looked at them. He saw that they were sincere and regretful. He felt sorry for them too. He smiled and gave them back their hats.
"Here you go, kids," he said. "I'm sorry I teased you too. I was just trying to show you how it feels. Teasing is not nice and not funny. It hurts people's feelings and makes them sad. You should be kind and respectful to everyone, even if they are different from you. That's the moral of the story."

She thought it was fun to make everything neat and tidy. Tom did not like to clean. He thought it was boring and hard. He liked to watch TV and play games on his phone.
One day, Lily asked Tom to help her clean the garden. There were many leaves and weeds and trash. Lily said, "Tom, please help me clean the garden. It will be faster and easier if we do it together. And then we can have a picnic and enjoy the sun."
Tom said, "No, Lily. I don't want to clean the garden. It is boring and hot. I want to watch TV and play games on my phone. You can clean the garden by yourself. I don't care."
Lily was sad and angry. She said, "Tom, you are lazy and selfish. You never help me with anything. You don't care about me or our house or our garden. You only care about yourself and your TV and your phone. I don't want to be married to you anymore. I want a divorce."
Tom was shocked and scared. He said, "Lily, don't say that. I love you. I don't want a divorce. I'm sorry. I will help you clean the garden. Please don't leave me."
But Lily did not listen. She said, "It is too late, Tom. You have hurt me too much. You have made me unhappy for too long. I don't love you anymore. I am leaving you. Goodbye, Tom."
Lily packed her bags and left the house. She took the car and drove away. Tom ran after her and cried. He said, "Lily, please come back. Please forgive me. Please don't go."
But Lily did not come back. She did not forgive him. She did not hear him. She was gone. Tom was alone. He had no wife, no house, no garden, no picnic, no sun. He only had his TV and his phone. And he was very, very sad. The end.

Tim and Sam are brothers. They like to play outside. One day, they find a big map in the attic. The map shows a treasure in the west.
"Let's go find the treasure!" Tim says.
"OK, but how do we go west?" Sam asks.
Tim points to the sun. "The sun goes down in the west. We can follow the sun."
They take the map and go outside. They step on the grass and the dirt. They see many things on the way: trees, flowers, birds, bugs, and rocks. They talk and laugh.
After a long time, they see a big hill. The sun is almost down. The map says the treasure is on the hill.
"Look, we are almost there!" Tim says.
"Wow, I wonder what the treasure is!" Sam says.
They run up the hill. They find a big box. It is old and rusty. They open the box. Inside, they see many regular things: books, toys, clothes, and pictures.
They are confused. They look at each other.
"Is this the treasure?" Tim asks.
"I guess so," Sam says.
They shrug. They pick some things they like. They put them in their pockets. They close the box.
They look at the sun. It is very red and pretty. They smile.
"Maybe the treasure is not the things in the box," Tim says.
"Maybe the treasure is the fun we had on the way," Sam says.
They hug. They go back home. They show their mom and dad what they found. They tell them about their adventure. They are happy.

Lily and Ben smile. They pet the bunny gently. The bunny lets them. It wiggles its nose. It makes a soft sound. Lily and Ben make the same sound. They laugh.

Lily and Tom were twins who liked to play together. One day, they found a big box in the garage. They decided to make it into a car and pretend to drive around. They cut out windows and doors and drew wheels and lights on the box.

"No, I want to be the driver!" Tom said.
They both grabbed the steering wheel and pulled hard. The box tore apart and they fell on the floor.
"Ow! You broke our car!" Lily cried.
"You broke it too!" Tom shouted.
They were both angry and sad. They did not want to play anymore.
Mom heard the noise and came to see what happened. She saw the broken box and the unhappy twins.
"What's going on here?" Mom asked.
"We were playing car, but we fought over who gets to drive and we broke it!" Lily said.
"That's not very nice. You should share and take turns. How would you feel if someone did that to you?" Mom said.
Lily and Tom thought about it. They realized they were not compassionate to each other. They felt sorry for what they did.
"We're sorry, Mom. We were selfish and mean. We should have been kind and fair." Lily said.
"We're sorry, too. We love each other and we don't want to fight. Can we fix the car and play again?" Tom said.
Mom smiled and hugged them. She helped them tape the box back together and gave them a new steering wheel.
"Of course you can. But remember, you have to share and take turns. And you have to be compassionate to each other and to others. That's how you show love and respect." Mom said.
Lily and Tom nodded and thanked Mom. They agreed to take turns driving the car and to let each other have a seat. They had fun playing car and learned a valuable lesson. They were happy and grateful.

She dreamed that a big monster was chasing her and trying to eat her. She was very scared and tried to run away, but the monster was faster and louder.
Anna woke up with a loud scream. She was shaking and sweating. She looked around and saw that it was only a nightmare. She hugged her teddy bear and reached for the light switch. But the light did not work. She tried again and again, but nothing happened. She was in the dark with her nightmare.
Anna started to cry. She cried so hard that her mom and dad heard her. They ran to her room and opened the door. They saw Anna crying and holding her teddy bear. They turned on the light and saw that the bulb was broken. They hugged Anna and told her that it was okay. They said that they were sorry that the light did not work and that they would fix it tomorrow. They said that they loved her and that they would stay with her until she fell asleep.
Anna felt better with her mom and dad. She told them about her nightmare and they said that it was not real. They said that monsters did not exist and that she was safe with them. They sang her a song and stroked her hair. Anna stopped crying and closed her eyes. She was not afraid of the dark anymore. She had her mom and dad and her teddy bear. She had no more nightmares that night. She had a good sleep.

"Her name is Sophie. She is your new sister. She can talk and sing and play with you. Do you like her?" daddy said.
Anna looked at Sophie. She looked at Lily. She felt something in her heart. She did not know what it was. She did not want to change her favorite doll. She did not want a new sister.
"I don't like her. I like Lily. Lily is my sister. Sophie is not. Take her away, daddy," Anna said.
Daddy looked sad. He did not expect Anna to say that. He wanted Anna to be happy. He wanted Anna to love Sophie.

Anna looked at daddy. She looked at Sophie. She saw Sophie's eyes. They were big and brown. They looked at Anna. They looked like they wanted to say something. Anna felt something in her heart. She did not know what it was. She felt curious. She felt sorry. She felt brave.
"Okay, daddy. I will try. Can I hold her?" Anna said.

"Hi, Sophie. I am Anna. I am your sister. I love you," Anna said.

Ben and Lily were playing with their toys in the garden. They had a big box of sand and some plastic animals and cars. They liked to make roads and hills and pretend they were on an adventure.
"Look, Lily, I made a volcano!" Ben said, pointing to a cone-shaped mound of sand. He had stuck a red bottle cap on top to make it look like lava. "It can melt anything with its fire!"
"Wow, Ben, that's cool!" Lily said, admiring his work. "Can I play with it too?"
"Sure, Lily, but be careful. The volcano is very hot and angry. It might explode!" Ben said, making a loud noise with his mouth.
Lily giggled and picked up a green dinosaur toy. She moved it closer to the volcano and said, "Roar! I'm a dinosaur and I'm not afraid of your volcano. I can eat it for breakfast!"
Ben gasped and said, "No, Lily, don't do that! The volcano will melt your dinosaur and make it go away!"
Lily pretended not to hear him and said, "Yum, yum, yum!" She pretended to bite the volcano with her dinosaur.
Suddenly, Ben grabbed a small bucket of water and poured it over the volcano. The sand collapsed and the bottle cap fell off. The water splashed on Lily and her dinosaur.
"Hey, Ben, what did you do that for?" Lily said, frowning and wiping her face.
"I saved your dinosaur, Lily. The volcano was going to melt it. See, it's gone now." Ben said, pointing to the ruined sand pile.
Lily looked at her wet dinosaur and then at Ben. She smiled and said, "Thank you, Ben. You're a good brother. But next time, can you make a nicer volcano? One that doesn't melt things?"
Ben nodded and said, "Okay, Lily. I'm sorry I made a scary volcano. Let's make a new one together. A red one, but a friendly one."
Lily hugged Ben and said, "Okay, Ben. I love you."
They hugged and then started to make a new volcano with their sand and toys. They played happily until their mom called them for lunch.

They heard Mom open the kitchen door. She gasped and said, "What happened here? Who did this?"
Ben and Lily stayed quiet in the closet. They hoped Mom would not find them. They wished they had not used the mixer. They wished they had made a nice cake for Mom. They wished they had not been so fat and hungry.

"OK," Lily said. "But be careful. The tree is very high."
They climbed the tree slowly and carefully. They saw many different birds. Some were red, some were blue, some were yellow. They heard the birds sing and chirp.
"This is interesting," Lily said. "The birds are so pretty and noisy."
"Look, I found a feather," Ben said. He held a long, green feather in his hand. "It is from a parrot. Do you want it?"
"Yes, please," Lily said. She took the feather and smiled. "Thank you, Ben. It is very nice."
Suddenly, they heard a loud squawk. They turned and saw a big, angry parrot. It was looking at them with its bright eyes.
"Hey, that's my feather," the parrot said. "Give it back to me. Now!"
Lily and Ben were scared. They did not know the parrot could talk. They dropped the feather and ran down the tree.
"Sorry, Mr. Parrot," Lily said. "We did not mean to take your feather."
"Yeah, sorry," Ben said. "We did not know it was yours."
The parrot flew down and picked up the feather. He put it back in his tail. He looked at Lily and Ben.
"Next time, ask before you take something," the parrot said. "But you are brave and curious. I like that. Do you want to be my friends?"
Lily and Ben nodded. They were still scared, but also curious.
"OK, then," the parrot said. "My name is Pete. What are your names?"
"I'm Lily," Lily said.
"I'm Ben," Ben said.
"Nice to meet you, Lily and Ben," Pete said. "Do you want to hear a story?"
"Yes, please," Lily and Ben said.
"OK, then," Pete said. "Let me reveal a secret to you. I was not always a parrot. I used to be a pirate."

Tom did not want to play pretend. He said, "No, Lily, I don't like spiders. They are not my friends. They are bad. Go away with your toy spider."
Lily said, "But Tom, this spider is not bad. He is just different. He has eight legs and eight eyes, but he also has a heart and feelings. He is weak because he is small and has no friends. He needs your help to find food and a home. Imagine how you would feel if you were him."
Tom thought for a moment. He tried to imagine how the spider would feel. He felt sorry for the spider. He said, "Okay, Lily, I will play pretend with you. But only for a little while. And don't put the spider on me."
Lily smiled and said, "Thank you, Tom. You are very brave and kind. Come on, let's play pretend. Imagine we are in a big forest and we have to help the spider find a safe place to live."
Tom and Lily played pretend with the toy spider. They had fun and learned more about spiders. Tom was not so afraid of spiders anymore. He realized they were not so scary or ugly or mean. They were just different. And sometimes, they needed a friend.

Sara loves animals. She has a dog, a cat, and a fish. She wants to be a veterinarian when she grows up. A veterinarian is a person who helps animals when they are sick or hurt.
One day, Sara's dog, Max, is not feeling well. He does not want to play or eat. He only lies on his bed and whines. Sara is worried. She tells her mom, "Mom, Max is sick. We need to take him to the veterinarian."
Mom nods and says, "Okay, Sara. Let's go to the car and drive to the veterinarian. Maybe he can make Max feel better."
They get in the car and drive to the veterinarian's office. There, they see a man in a white coat. He smiles and says, "Hello, I am Dr. Lee. I am a veterinarian. Who is this?"
Sara says, "This is Max. He is my dog. I love him very much. But he is sick. Can you help him?"
Dr. Lee says, "Of course, Sara. I will examine Max and see what is wrong. Maybe he has a fever or a tummy ache. Don't worry, I will be gentle and kind."
He takes Max to a room and checks his ears, eyes, nose, mouth, and belly. He gives him a shot and some medicine. He says, "Good boy, Max. You are very brave. The shot and the medicine will make you feel better soon. You just need to rest and drink some water."
He brings Max back to Sara and Mom. He says, "Max is fine. He had a mild infection, but the shot and the medicine will clear it up. He should be back to his normal self in a day or two. Just keep an eye on him and give him lots of love."
Sara hugs Max and says, "Thank you, Dr. Lee. You are a good veterinarian. You helped Max. I am glad."
Dr. Lee says, "You are welcome, Sara. You are a good owner. You care for Max. I am glad too."
Sara, Mom, and Max go back to the car and drive home. Sara says, "Mom, I want to be a veterinarian like Dr. Lee when I grow up. I want to help animals like he does."
Mom says, "That is a wonderful dream, Sara. I am proud of you. You have a big heart and a smart mind. You can be anything you want to be."

"Really?" Sam and Tom asked. "What happened to it?"

Sam and Tom smiled and said, "You're welcome. We are happy to share. Sharing is caring."
The elderly man sailed the boat in the pond and enjoyed it very much. He said, "You are right. Sharing is caring. And caring is happiness."

"And I am the queen!" Lily said. She wore a necklace of flowers and berries.

"Oh no, there is a fire in the woods!" Lily said. She was scared.
"Let's go and see if we can help!" Ben said. He was brave.
They ran to the woods and saw a small fire near some dry leaves and branches. They also saw a man with a bucket of water. He was trying to put out the fire.
"Hello, can we help you?" Ben asked.
"Hello, thank you for coming. I am a ranger and I watch over the woods. Someone left a campfire here and it started to spread. Can you help me bring some more water from the stream?" the man said.
"Sure, we can do that!" Lily said.
They followed the man to the stream and filled their buckets with water. Then they ran back to the fire and poured the water on it. They did this several times, until the fire was gone.
"Thank you, you are very kind and helpful. You saved the woods and the animals from the fire. You are true heroes!" the man said.
He gave them each a badge with a picture of a tree and a bird.
Lily and Ben were very happy and proud. They hugged the man and thanked him.
They went back to their rock and looked at the woods. They saw the green trees, the blue sky, and the colorful birds. They felt peaceful and grateful.
They learned that playing is fun, but helping is important. They also learned that fire can be dangerous, and they should be careful with it. They decided to always respect and protect the woods and the animals. They were good twins.

Sam and Lily liked to play in the park. They liked to swing, slide and run. One day, they saw a big truck near the park. The truck had a long cable. The cable went up to a tall tree.
"What is that?" Sam asked.
"I don't know," Lily said. "Maybe they are fixing the tree."
They went closer to the truck. They saw a man with a big hat and a big saw. He was cutting the tree. He did not see Sam and Lily.
"Look, he is making the tree smaller," Sam said.
"Why is he doing that?" Lily asked.
"Maybe the tree is sick. Or maybe he wants to make something with the wood."
They watched the man for a while. Then they heard a loud noise. The tree fell down. The cable snapped. The cable flew in the air. It came towards Sam and Lily.
"Watch out!" the man shouted.
Sam and Lily were scared. They ran away from the cable. But the cable was faster. It hit Sam on the leg. Sam fell down. He cried.
"Sam, are you okay?" Lily asked.
She ran to Sam. She hugged him. She saw blood on his leg.
"Help! Help!" she yelled.
The man ran to them. He saw Sam's leg. He was sorry.
"I'm sorry, kids. I didn't see you. Are you hurt?"
Sam nodded. He was hurt. He was in pain.
The man took out his phone. He called for help.
"Don't worry, kids. Help is coming. You will be okay."
He gave Sam a bandage. He gave Lily a candy. He tried to make them feel better.
Soon, a big car with a red light and a loud sound came. The car had people who could help Sam. They put Sam on a bed. They took him to the car.
"Lily, do you want to come with Sam?" one of the people asked.
Lily nodded. She wanted to be with Sam. She was his friend.
She got in the car. She held Sam's hand. She told him a story. She made him smile.
The car took them to a place where they could fix Sam's leg. It was not easy. But Sam was brave. Lily was brave too.
They stayed in the place for a while. Then they went home. They were happy. They were safe.
They learned a lesson. They learned to be careful. They learned to stay away from big trucks and cables. They learned to listen to people who knew more than them.
They still liked to play in the park. But they never went near the truck again.

"What can I do?" asked Frank.
His dad smiled. "Stretch out your finger, like this," he said, extending his hand.
Frank tried to stretch out his finger, but he couldn't.
"Let me help you," said his dad, and he opened Frank's fingers one-by-one.
Frank now had a long, open finger. He was able to pick the apples easily!
Frank and his dad had a great time at the park and they collected lots of apples to take home.

John was so excited to go to the beach. He was walking on the sand, feeling the gentle breeze... when suddenly, he saw a huge wave rising in the distance. 
He was scared and asked his mom: "Mom, why is that wave rising?" 
"That's the tide coming in!" said his mom, "It often gets bigger when the tide is high. We need to be quiet so it doesn't come close to us."
John saw how the tide got bigger, but he was still curious. He took his board and slowly walked farther away to get a better look. His mom watched him, but stayed quiet.
John slowly got closer to the waves. The waves were crashing and roaring. But he was fearless and kept going. Finally, he was close enough to feel the wetness of the sea on his skin. He felt the water rising beneath his board, and he was so excited to be there. 
He looked back and saw his mom smiling. The tide had risen, but John felt proud of himself for facing his fear and going closer to it.

Once upon a time there was a small fat seal who lived by the sea shore. Every day, she would lay in the sun and measure how much time had passed. One day, a huge wave came to the shore and washed her away to a small pond. The seal was now stuck in the pond and her only way out was up a slippery rock.
The seal tried to measure the rock with her eyes, but it was too high. She tried to climb up, but her soft, fat body made it hard. With all her strength, she managed to climb halfway up the rock, but kept slipping back down. The seal began to cry in frustration.
Just then, a small voice said, “I can help you, little seal”. The voice belonged to a kind old turtle who was watching from the safety of the pond. He said, “If you measure one small step at a time, you will be able to reach the top.”
The seal thought about this advice and tried to take it one small step at a time. She was soon at the top of the rock! She thanked the turtle for his help and waddled back safely to the shore.
The moral of this story is that sometimes tackling something big is easier if we break it down into smaller achievable steps.

Suddenly, the spaceship opened and out stepped an alien! John couldn't believe his eyes. He had never seen anything like it before!
The alien spoke to John in a language he couldn't understand. It waved its hands around and motioned for John to come closer. Even though he was a bit scared, John stepped closer and eventually he started to understand what the alien was trying to tell him.
John was so happy that he was able to understand the alien. They hugged and talked for a while until the alien had to go back to its spaceship. 
The alien never came again, but that afternoon John was very happy. He knew he had experienced something special and he would always remember it.

Lily saw a puddle on the ground. She wanted to jump in it, but her mommy said, "No, Lily. You will get wet." Lily listened to her mommy and didn't jump in the puddle.
As they crossed the road, Lily saw a little boy who didn't wait for the light to turn green. He ran across the road and almost got hit by a car. Lily's mommy said, "That boy didn't listen to his mommy. He didn't wait for the light to turn green. He could have gotten hurt."
Lily learned that it's important to listen to her mommy and wait for the light to turn green before crossing the road. She was happy she didn't get wet in the puddle and was safe.

A friendly cat heard the lady cry and went to her house. The cat said, "Do not cry, lady. I am here to help you." The lady looked at the cat and asked, "Can you make the dark go away?" The cat thought for a moment and then said, "I cannot make the dark go away, but I can stay with you until the sun rises again."
The nervous lady felt a little better with the cat by her side. They sat by the window and watched the moon rise higher and higher. The cat tried to make the lady laugh with funny faces, but the lady was still very scared. She could not stop thinking about the big shadow outside.
As the night went on, the lady and the cat heard a loud noise outside. The lady was so scared that she hid under the bed. The cat tried to tell her that it was just the wind, but the lady did not believe her. She stayed under the bed, shaking with fear.
The sun never rose again for the nervous lady. She stayed under the bed, too scared to come out. The cat tried to help her, but the lady was too scared of the dark. The cat left the house, feeling sad that she could not help the lady. And the nervous lady stayed under the bed, scared of the dark forever.

Love, Santa

One day, their mom told them to tidy their room before they could play with the rocket. She said, "You have to put your toys in the box and your clothes in the closet. Then you can have fun with the rocket. I will remind you in ten minutes."
Tom and Lily nodded, but they did not listen. They ran to the rocket and started to play. They forgot about their mom and their room. They had so much fun that they did not hear their mom calling them.
Their mom came to their room and saw the mess. She was angry and sad. She said, "You did not tidy your room. You did not do what I asked you. You did not listen to me. Now you cannot play with the rocket. You have to put it away and clean your room."
Tom and Lily were sorry and sad. They realized they made a mistake. They said, "We are sorry, mom. We were naughty. We should have listened to you. We should have tidied our room. Please, can we play with the rocket later?"
Their mom said, "You can play with the rocket later, but only if you tidy your room first. And you have to promise to listen to me next time. I remind you because I love you and I want you to be good and happy."
Tom and Lily hugged their mom and said, "We love you, mom. We promise to listen to you. We will tidy our room now. Thank you for reminding us."
They put their toys in the box and their clothes in the closet. They made their bed and swept the floor. They made their room tidy and nice. Then they played with the rocket and had fun. They learned to listen to their mom and to be tidy. They were good and happy.

Grandpa put down his book and smiled. He took the shiny thing from Anna and looked at it closely.
"Well, well, well, what do we have here?" he said. "This is a very old and special tool, Anna. This is a coin. A very old coin. Do you know what a coin is?"
Anna shook her head. She had never seen a coin before.
"A coin is a piece of metal that people use to buy things. Like candy, or toys, or books. But this coin is very old. It is from a long time ago, when people used different coins than we do now. This coin is very rare and valuable. You are very lucky to find it, Anna. You have made a great discovery."
Anna's eyes widened. She did not understand all the words that Grandpa said, but she understood that the shiny thing was important and good. She felt happy and proud.
"Wow, Grandpa, thank you for telling me. Can I keep the coin? Can I show it to Mommy and Daddy?"
"Of course you can, Anna. It is your coin. You found it. You can show it to anyone you want. But be careful, don't lose it or let Spot eat it. It is a very precious tool. And you are a very clever girl."
Anna hugged Grandpa and thanked him. She put the coin in her pocket and ran to find Mommy and Daddy. She wanted to tell them about her discovery and show them her tool. She was very happy. And so was Spot, who followed her, hoping for a treat.

"Wow, that's amazing!" Mia said. "The wheat shrank and changed!"
"That's right," the farmer said. "The mill grinds the wheat and makes it into flour. Then we can use the flour to bake bread and cakes and pies. Do you like bread and cakes and pies?"
"Yes, we do!" Tim and Mia said, hungry.
"Then come with me," the farmer said. "I have some fresh ones in the kitchen. You can have a slice if you like."

One day, Lily found a big worm in the dirt. She picked it up and put it in her hand. She wanted to show it to her mom. But the worm did not like to be in her hand. It tried to wriggle away. Lily held it too tight. She did not want to lose it.
The worm started to change. It became hard and stiff and brown. It did not move anymore. Lily was scared. She did not know what happened to the worm. She ran to her mom and showed her the worm.
Mom looked at the worm and smiled. She said, "Lily, this is not a worm. This is a caterpillar. Caterpillars are delicate. They can change into butterflies. But they need to be in a safe place to do that. You hurt the caterpillar when you held it too tight. Next time, be gentle with the caterpillars. They are living things, like you and me."
Lily felt sorry for the caterpillar. She said, "I'm sorry, caterpillar. I did not mean to hurt you. I hope you can change into a butterfly and fly away." She put the caterpillar back in the dirt and said goodbye. She learned to be careful with the creatures in the garden. She hoped to see a butterfly someday.

Lily likes to sign. She signs with her hands and her face. She signs hello, thank you, and I love you. She signs to her mom and dad, and to her friends at school. She signs because she cannot hear, but she can see and feel.
One day, Lily goes to the park with her mom. She sees a woman on a bench. The woman has a book and a dog. The woman smiles at Lily and signs hello. Lily is surprised and happy. She signs hello back. The woman signs her name. It is Anna. Lily signs her name too.
Lily and Anna talk with their hands. They talk about the book, the dog, and the park. They talk about their favorite colors, animals, and foods. They laugh and have fun. Lily thinks Anna is charming. She likes her eyes, her hair, and her dress. She likes her voice, even if she cannot hear it.
Lily's mom watches them. She is glad that Lily has a new friend. She thinks Anna is charming too. She likes her kindness, her patience, and her smile. She likes her sign language, even if she cannot speak it.
Lily and Anna say goodbye. They sign see you soon, and hug. Lily and her mom go home. Lily tells her mom about Anna. She signs she is charming. Her mom agrees. She signs she is charming too. They sign I love you, and hug.

Lily was a dog who liked to run and play in the park. She had a lot of friends, like Ben the cat, Sam the squirrel and Max the bird. They always had fun together, chasing balls, climbing trees and singing songs.
One day, Lily felt something itchy on her fur. She scratched and scratched, but it did not help. She looked and saw a tiny bug on her back. It was a flea. The flea was very hungry and bit Lily hard. Lily yelped and shook her fur, but the flea did not fall off.
"Ouch, ouch, ouch!" Lily cried. "Who are you and why are you hurting me?"
The flea laughed and said, "I am Fred, the most intelligent flea in the world. I have traveled to many places and learned many things. I can speak any language, solve any puzzle and tell any joke. And I am hungry, so I need to lend some of your blood."
Lily did not like Fred at all. She did not think he was intelligent, she thought he was mean and rude. She did not want to lend him her blood, she wanted him to leave her alone. She asked her friends for help.
"Ben, Sam, Max, please help me. There is a flea on my back who bites me and says he is intelligent. How can I get rid of him?"
Ben, Sam and Max looked at Lily and saw the flea. They did not like Fred either. They wanted to help Lily. They thought of a plan.
"Fred, if you are so intelligent, we have a challenge for you," Ben said. "We have a ball here that has a riddle on it. If you can read the riddle and answer it, we will let you stay on Lily. But if you cannot, you have to leave her alone. Do you accept?"
Fred was very confident. He thought he could read and answer any riddle. He agreed to the challenge. He jumped off Lily and landed on the ball. He looked at the riddle. It said:
What has four legs but does not walk?
Fred was puzzled. He tried to think of an answer, but he could not. He scratched his head and said, "I don't know. What is it?"
Ben, Sam and Max smiled and said, "A table!"
Fred felt very silly. He had failed the challenge. He had to leave Lily alone. He was ashamed and angry. He hopped off the ball and ran away.
Lily was very happy. She thanked her friends for helping her. She said, "You are the most intelligent and kind friends in the world. I am glad you are here."
They hugged and said, "You are welcome, Lily. We are glad you are here too."
They continued to play and have fun in the park, without any fleas.

Tom and Mia love to watch cartoons on TV. They like the ones with powerful heroes who can speed and fly and fight bad guys. They have a big box of toys with many heroes and villains. Sometimes they play with them and make their own stories.
One day, they decided to make a big race with their toys. They used a long rug as the road and put some pillows and books as obstacles. They each picked their favorite hero and put them in a small car. Tom chose Superboy, who had a red cape and a blue suit. Mia chose Wondergirl, who had a golden rope and a star on her chest.
"Are you ready?" Tom asked. "My Superboy is the fastest and strongest. He will win for sure."
"No way!" Mia said. "My Wondergirl is smarter and braver. She will beat your Superboy."
They counted to three and pushed their cars. The cars zoomed along the rug, dodging the pillows and books. Tom and Mia cheered and shouted for their heroes. They were having so much fun.
But then, something happened. Superboy's car hit a big book and flipped over. Wondergirl's car got stuck in a pillow. Both heroes fell out of their cars and landed on the floor.
"Oh no!" Tom and Mia said. They ran to their toys and picked them up. They looked at each other and smiled.
"It's OK," Tom said. "They are both powerful. They can get up and try again."
"Yes," Mia said. "They are both good. They can help each other and be friends."
They hugged their toys and put them back in their cars. They decided to finish the race together. They pushed their cars slowly and carefully, making sure they did not crash again. They crossed the end of the rug at the same time.
"Hooray!" Tom and Mia said. "We are all winners!"
They turned off the TV and put their toys back in the box. They were happy and tired. They gave each other a high five and went to have a snack. They agreed that playing with cartoons was more fun than watching them.

Once upon a time, there was a silly monkey named Bongo. Bongo loved to eat bananas and swing from tree to tree. One day, Bongo saw a shiny car driving down the road. 
"Wow! That car is so cool!" Bongo exclaimed. "What makes it go?"
"It needs fuel to run," replied the driver of the car.
Bongo blinked his eyes in surprise. "Fuel? What's that?"
"It's like food for the car. Just like you need bananas to have energy, the car needs fuel to move," explained the driver.
Bongo thought for a moment, then asked, "Can I put bananas in the car instead of fuel?"
The driver chuckled. "No, I'm afraid not. That would be silly! The car needs special fuel to run."
Bongo laughed and continued swinging from tree to tree, dreaming of the day he could ride in a shiny car powered by bananas.

Ben followed them and sat next to Lily. He saw a fish lying on the grass. It was the fish that had jumped out of the water to get Lily's bread. It was not moving.
"Mom, look, a fish!" Ben said. He pointed to the fish.
"Oh, poor fish. It was too greedy. It jumped out of the water and now it can't breathe," Mom said.
"Can we help it, Mom?" Lily asked. She stopped crying and looked at the fish.
"I'm afraid not, Lily. It's too late. The fish is dead," Mom said.
"Dead?" Ben and Lily asked. They did not understand what dead meant.
"It means the fish is not alive anymore. It can't swim or eat or play. It's very sad," Mom said.
"Sad," Ben and Lily repeated. They felt sorry for the fish.
"Maybe we can bury it, Mom. Then it can lie in the ground and rest," Ben suggested.
"That's a good idea, Ben. Let's find a spot to bury the fish. Then we can say goodbye to it," Mom said.
They found a shady spot under a tree. Mom dug a hole with a stick. Ben and Lily put the fish in the hole and covered it with dirt. They found some flowers and stones and decorated the grave.
"Goodbye, fish. We're sorry you were unlucky. We hope you're happy in the ground," Ben and Lily said.
"Goodbye, fish. Thank you for teaching us a lesson. We will be careful and not greedy," Mom said.
They said a prayer and left the fish to lie in peace. They went back to the pond and fed the other fish. They were more gentle and generous. They learned to be happy with what they had. They were lucky.

Lily liked to play the piano. She had a big piano in her room. She played songs every day. She played when she was happy, when she was sad, when she was bored. She played loud and soft, fast and slow, high and low.
One night, Lily had a bad dream. She dreamed that a monster came and took her piano away. She woke up and cried. She ran to her room and looked for her piano. It was still there. She hugged it and said, "I love you, piano. You are my best friend."
She wanted to play a song to make herself feel better. But it was very dark and very quiet. Everyone else was sleeping. Lily thought, "Maybe I can play a little bit. Just one song. No one will hear me."
She turned on the lamp and sat on the stool. She put her fingers on the keys and pressed them. The piano made a loud noise. It sounded like thunder. Lily was scared. She stopped playing.
But it was too late. She woke up her mom and dad and her baby brother. They came to her room and saw her with the piano. They were not happy. They were angry and tired.
"Why are you playing the piano at night?" her mom asked. "You know you have to be quiet when everyone is sleeping. You are being very rude and selfish. You are not thinking of others. You are only thinking of yourself."
Lily felt sorry. She did not mean to wake them up. She did not mean to be rude or selfish. She just wanted to play the piano. She liked the piano. But she liked her family more. She said, "I'm sorry, mom. I'm sorry, dad. I'm sorry, baby brother. I had a bad dream and I wanted to play the piano. But I should have waited until morning. I should have been more careful and respectful. I won't do it again. Please forgive me."
Her mom and dad and her baby brother hugged her and said, "We forgive you, Lily. We love you, too. But next time, please remember that the piano is not the only thing that matters. There are other people who need your love and care. And there are other ways to express your feelings. You can talk to us, or draw a picture, or read a book, or cuddle with your teddy bear. The piano is a wonderful gift, but it is not the only gift. You have to share it and use it wisely."
Lily nodded and smiled. She learned her lesson. She said, "Thank you, mom. Thank you, dad. Thank you, baby brother. You are right. The piano is a wonderful gift, but it is not the only gift. I have to share it and use it wisely. And I have to be quiet when everyone is sleeping. I love you all very much."
They kissed her good night and turned off the lamp. Lily went back to bed and closed her eyes. She dreamed of playing the piano in the morning, with her family listening and clapping. She was happy. She slept well.

Tim did not care. He liked the doll. It had a smooth dress and a long cord for hair. He pulled the cord and made the doll's hair shorter.
"Stop it!" Lily cried. "You are hurting my doll!"
Mom heard Lily's cry. She came to see what was wrong. She saw Tim with the doll and Lily with the car.
"Tim, what did you do?" Mom asked. "You cut the doll's hair! That is very bad!"
Tim felt ashamed. He saw Lily's tears and the doll's hair. He realized he was wrong. He gave the doll back to Lily and said he was sorry.
"I am sorry, Lily. I was mean. I should not have taken your doll. Here, you can have it back. And you can have my car too."
Lily stopped weeping. She smiled and hugged Tim. She thanked him and gave him back his car.
"Thank you, Tim. I forgive you. You are a good brother. I love you."
Mom was proud of Tim and Lily. She hugged them both and said they were good children. She told them they should always be kind and share with each other. She said that was the right thing to do.

"Sorry, Tom," Lily says. "I was hungry. Do you want to play again?"
Tom laughs. He is not mad. He likes Lily. He says, "OK, but this time I will hide the box. And I will not eat the mints. I promise."

The duck is happy. He has stopped the noise and the engines. He swims away, quacking.

Lila and Ben were twins, but they were very different. Lila liked to draw and sing, and Ben liked to build and run. They had unique toys and clothes, and they did not like to share.

"Ouch, ouch, ouch!" Ben complained. "The soup is too hot! I don't want it!"
"Shh, shh, shh!" Lila said. "The soup is good! You have to wait a little bit. Then it will be just right!"
But Ben did not want to wait. He pushed his bowl away and crossed his arms. He looked at Lila's bowl and saw that she had more carrots than him.
"Hey, hey, hey!" Ben said. "That's not fair! You have more carrots than me! I want some of your carrots!"
"No, no, no!" Lila said. "These are my carrots! You have your own soup! You can't have mine!"
They started to argue and shout. Their mom heard them and came to the kitchen. She saw the twins fighting over the soup and the steam.
"What is going on here?" she asked. "Why are you complaining and yelling? Don't you like the soup I made for you?"
Lila and Ben stopped and looked at their mom. They felt sorry for making her sad. They knew she worked hard to make the soup for them.
"We're sorry, mom," they said together. "We do like the soup. We were just being silly."
They hugged their mom and thanked her for the soup. Then they ate their soup quietly and happily. They even shared some of their carrots. They learned that soup is better when it is not too hot, and when it is shared with love.

But then they heard a loud noise. It was Max, the mean boy. He saw the club and ran towards it. He wanted to break it.
"Hey, what is this?" Max shouted. "This is a weak club. I can smash it with my foot."
Sam and Lily were scared. They did not want Max to ruin their club. They did not want Max to hurt them.
"Go away, Max!" Sam yelled. "This is our club. You are not nice. You are not welcome."
Max laughed. He did not care. He kicked the club hard. The leaves and the small sticks flew away. The big stick fell down. The club was gone.

Max saw them crying. He felt bad. He realized he was wrong. He did not want to make them cry.

Sam and Lily looked at Max. They saw he was sorry. They decided to forgive him.
"Okay, Max," Sam said. "You can help us. But you have to be nice. And you have to share."
Max nodded. He agreed. He helped them find new sticks and leaves. He helped them make a new club. He played with them inside. He shared his toys and snacks.
They all became friends. They all had fun. They all liked the club.

One day, they decided to play music at the park. Lily banged her drum loudly and Sam blew his whistle softly. They made a brilliant sound that they both enjoyed. But not everyone liked their music. A big boy named Max came over and said, "Stop that noise! You are hurting my ears!"
Lily and Sam were scared of Max. He was much bigger and stronger than them. He grabbed Lily's drum and threw it on the ground. He snatched Sam's whistle and put it in his pocket. He laughed and said, "Now you can't play music anymore. Go away!"
Lily and Sam were very sad and angry. They wanted their drum and whistle back. They did not know what to do. They looked around and saw a lady sitting on a bench. The lady looked up and saw Max. She frowned and said, "That's not nice. He should not take things that are not his. Come with me. I will talk to him." She got up and took Lily and Sam by the hand. She walked to Max and said, "Hello, I am Mrs. Lee. I am a teacher at the school. I saw what you did to these children. Why did you do that?"
Max was surprised and nervous. He did not know that the lady was a teacher. He did not like teachers. He said, "I don't know. I just wanted to have some fun. I don't like their music. It's too loud and silly."
Mrs. Lee said, "Well, fun is good, but not when it hurts others. Their music is not loud and silly. It's brilliant and creative. They have a right to play music. And you have no right to take their drum and whistle. That's stealing and that's wrong. You need to apologize and give them back."
Max felt ashamed and sorry. He realized that he was wrong. He said, "I'm sorry. I was mean and rude. Here is your drum and whistle. Please forgive me." He gave Lily and Sam their drum and whistle back.
Lily and Sam smiled and said, "Thank you. We forgive you. Do you want to play music with us? We can share our drum and whistle. It's more fun when we play together."
Max nodded and said, "Yes, I would like that. Thank you for being kind to me. Maybe I can learn to play music too." He joined Lily and Sam and they played music together. "Oh no!" Tom said. "The leaves are on fire!"
They saw the flame grow bigger and bigger. It made a lot of smoke and noise. They were scared and ran to the house. They told their mom what happened.
Mom was very angry and worried. She called the firemen. They came with a big red truck and a loud siren. They used water to put out the fire. They told Tom and Lily that matches are very dangerous and they should never play with them.
"I'm sorry, Mom," Tom said. "I didn't know it would make a fire."
"Me too, Mom," Lily said. "I was just curious."
Mom hugged them and said, "I'm glad you're safe, but you have to be careful. Matches can strike a flame and start a fire. Fire can burn things and hurt people. You have to listen to me and never touch matches again. Do you understand?"
"Yes, Mom," Tom and Lily said. "We understand."
They learned their lesson and never played with matches again. They found other ways to have fun in the yard.

The bunnies hopped along the path, and came upon a clearing. In the clearing was a patch of carrot seeds. The bunnies were very excited. They started to scatter the carrot seeds in the grass. Then they hopped away, eager to see the carrots grow.
The bunnies went back to the meadow every day to check on the carrots. Finally, one day, their hard work paid off – the carrots were ready to pick! The bunnies dug out the carrots and the air filled with the scent of victory.
 
From then on, whenever the bunnies saw a zigzag path, they followed it, hoping to find more seeds to scatter.

One day, Ben sees a new girl next door. She has a bike. It is pink and has two wheels and a basket. She likes to ride it on the sidewalk and ring a bell. She thinks her bike is unique. No one else has a bike like hers.
Ben wants to play with the girl. He drives his jeep to her fence and says hello. The girl stops her bike and says hello back. Ben asks her what her name is. She says her name is Mia. Ben tells her his name and says he likes her bike. Mia says she likes his jeep.
"Do you want to play with me?" Ben asks. "I can bring my jeep to your yard."
"OK," Mia says. "I can bring my bike to your yard too. Then we can share and try each other's toys."
Ben and Mia smile. They bring their toys to each other's yards and have fun. They learn that their toys are unique, but they are not so different. They become good friends.

Lily and Ben were playing with their toy animals on the floor. They had a big elephant, a small mouse, a loud lion and a quiet rabbit. Lily liked the elephant best, because it was big and strong. Ben liked the mouse best, because it was small and fast.
"Let's weigh our animals," Lily said. "I bet my elephant is the heaviest."
"Okay," Ben said. "How do we weigh them?"
Lily thought for a moment. She saw a big book on the table. She got up and dragged the book to the floor. "We can use this book as a scale," she said. "We put one animal on each side and see which side goes down."
They put the elephant on one side of the book and the mouse on the other side. The book tilted down on the elephant's side. "See, my elephant is heavier than your mouse," Lily said.
"Let's try another pair," Ben said. He took the lion and the rabbit and put them on the book. The book tilted down on the lion's side. "My lion is heavier than your rabbit," Ben said.
They tried all the pairs of animals and saw which ones were heavier and which ones were lighter. They had fun comparing their animals and making noises like them.
Then they heard a gentle voice from the door. It was their mom. "What are you two doing?" she asked.
"We are weighing our animals, mom," Lily said. "We are using this book as a scale."
"That's very clever," mom said. "But it's time for a snack now. Come and wash your hands."
Lily and Ben put their animals back in their basket and followed mom to the kitchen. They were hungry and happy. They liked playing with their animals and learning new things.

Anna and Ben were very excite to go to the party. They put on their mask and their best clothes. Anna had a pink mask with flowers and Ben had a blue mask with stars.
"Let's go, let's go!" Ben said. He wanted to see his friends and play games.
"Wait, Ben, we have to say bye to Mom and Dad," Anna said. She was more careful and polite.
"Bye, Mom, bye, Dad, we love you!" they said and hugged their parents.
"Have fun, but be good, okay?" Mom said. "Don't be naughty or you will miss the cake."
"Okay, Mom, we promise," they said and ran to the car.
At the party, there were many other kids with mask and costumes. They played, danced, sang, and laughed. Anna and Ben had a lot of fun.
But then, Ben saw a big bowl of candy on the table. He wanted to eat some, but he remembered what Mom said.
"Anna, look, candy!" he whispered. "Can we have some?"
"I don't know, Ben, maybe we should ask first," Anna said. She was not sure if it was for everyone or just for the birthday kid.
"Come on, Anna, just one, no one will notice," Ben said. He was very tempted and curious.
He reached for the bowl and grabbed a handful of candy. He put some in his mouth and some in his pocket.
"Ben, stop, that's naughty!" Anna said. She was worried and scared.
But it was too late. The birthday kid saw Ben and shouted.
"Hey, that's my candy! You stole it! You're a bad kid!"
Everyone looked at Ben and his mask. He felt ashamed and sorry.
He spit out the candy and said.
"I'm sorry, I'm sorry, I didn't mean to. Please forgive me."
He gave back the candy and took off his mask. He looked at Anna and she looked at him.
They both felt sad and wanted to go home. They learned a lesson that day.
The end.

Lily and Sam were friends who liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a new boy sitting on a bench. He looked sad and lonely. Lily and Sam wanted to help him.
"Hi, I am Lily and this is Sam. What is your name?" Lily asked the boy.
The boy looked up and smiled a little. "I am Ben. I just moved here with my mom and dad. I don't know anyone here."
"We can be your friends. Do you want to play with us?" Sam said.
Ben nodded and got up from the bench. Lily and Sam took him to the swings, the slide and the sandbox. They had a lot of fun together. Then, they saw a big rope hanging from a tree.
"Look, a rope! We can swing on it!" Lily said.
She ran to the rope and grabbed it. She swung back and forth, laughing. "This is so fun! Come on, Ben, you try!"
Ben was scared of the rope. He had never swung on a rope before. He thought he might fall and hurt himself. He shook his head and backed away.
"It's okay, Ben. You don't have to swing if you don't want to. We can do something else." Sam said.
He took Ben's hand and led him to the grass. They lay down and looked at the clouds. They saw shapes of animals, cars and stars. They talked and giggled.
Lily joined them after a while. She saw that Ben was happy and relaxed. She was glad that he was having a good time. She was grateful that she and Sam had introduced themselves to him. She hoped that they would be friends for a long time.
The end.

Tom and Sue wanted to go on the water in a kayak. A kayak is a long boat that you sit in and move with a stick that has a flat part on each end. They asked their dad if they could borrow his kayak, and he said yes, but they had to be careful and not spoil it.
They took the kayak to the lake and put it in the water. They put on life jackets and got in the kayak. They had fun paddling around and looking at the fish and the birds. They saw another kayak with two kids in it. The kids waved at them and said hello.
"Hi, do you want to race?" one of the kids asked.
"Sure, we like to race!" Tom said.
"OK, let's go to that big rock over there and back. Ready, set, go!" the other kid said.
Tom and Sue paddled as fast as they could, but the other kayak was faster. They got to the rock first and turned around. Tom and Sue tried to catch up, but they were too far behind.
"Ha ha, we win, we win!" the other kids shouted.
They were so happy that they did not see a big branch sticking out of the water. They hit the branch with their kayak and made a big hole in it. Water started to get in the kayak and make it sink.
"Help, help, we're sinking!" the other kids cried.
Tom and Sue saw what happened and paddled to them. They helped them get out of the kayak and onto the shore. They were wet and scared, but not hurt.
"Thank you, thank you, you saved us!" the other kids said.
"You're welcome, but what about your kayak? It's spoiled now. How will you tell your dad?" Sue asked.
The other kids looked at the kayak and started to cry.
"We don't know, we don't know. We were ignorant. We did not look where we were going. We were too busy showing off. We're sorry, we're sorry!" they said.
Tom and Sue felt sorry for them, but they also felt glad that they did not spoil their dad's kayak. They learned a lesson that day: it is better to be careful and kind than to be fast and rude.

Jen has an old truck. It is blue and rusty. It has a small horn and a short trailer. Jen says, "Your truck is not so great. My truck is better. It can deliver anything smooth and quiet!"
Tim and Jen want to see who has the best truck. They make a race. They put some toys in their trailers. They say, "Ready, set, go!"
Tim drives his truck fast. He pushes the horn. He makes a lot of noise. He goes over bumps and rocks. He makes his truck jump and shake. He says, "My truck is the best! It has a lot of speed! It can deliver anything rough!"
Jen drives her truck slow. She pulls the horn. She makes a little noise. She goes around bumps and rocks. She makes her truck glide and sway. She says, "My truck is the best! It has a lot of skill! It can deliver anything gentle!"
Tim and Jen reach the end of the race. They look at their trailers. Tim's trailer is empty. All his toys have fallen out. Jen's trailer is full. All her toys are still there.
Tim says, "Oh no! My truck is too fast and loud! It cannot deliver anything rough!"
Jen says, "Ha ha! My truck is just right and quiet! It can deliver anything gentle!"
Tim and Jen learn a lesson. They say, "Maybe both our trucks are good. They can deliver different things. We can share our trucks and toys. We can be friends and drivers!"

Ben did not like cauliflower. It was white and hard and had a bad smell. He pushed it away on his plate and made a face.
"Ben, you have to eat your cauliflower. It is good for you," his mom said.
"No, mom, I don't want it. It is yucky," Ben said.
"Please, Ben, just try one bite. If you don't eat it, you can't have dessert," his mom said.
Ben looked at the dessert. It was a big slice of chocolate cake with cream and sprinkles. He wanted it very much. But he did not want the cauliflower.
He had an idea. He took a big spoon and scooped up some cauliflower. He pretended to put it in his mouth, but he really hid it under his napkin. He did this again and again until his plate was empty.
"See, mom, I ate all my cauliflower. Can I have cake now?" he said.
His mom smiled and gave him a piece of cake. Ben was happy. He ate the cake and licked his fingers. It was sweet and soft and had a good taste.
But then he felt something cold and wet on his lap. He looked down and saw his napkin. It was full of cauliflower and it had fallen off his plate. The cauliflower was cold and soggy and had a worse smell.
His mom saw it too. She was not happy. She took away his cake and said, "Ben, you lied to me. You did not eat your cauliflower. You hid it under your napkin. That is not nice. You have to leave the table and go to your room. No more cake for you."
Ben was sad. He cried and said, "I'm sorry, mom. I don't like cauliflower. Please, can I have some cake?"
But his mom said, "No, Ben. You have to learn your lesson. Maybe next time you will eat your cauliflower. Now go to your room and think about what you did."
Ben left the table and went to his room. He wished he had eaten his cauliflower. He wished he had not lied to his mom. He wished he had some cake. He did not like cauliflower. But he liked cake. And he liked his mom. He hoped she would forgive him. He said, "I'm sorry, mom. I love you."

Tom and Amy are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big book on a bench. The book has many pictures and words. Tom picks up the book and says, "Look, Amy, this is a history book. It tells us about things that happened a long time ago."
Amy is curious. She asks, "What is history, Tom?"
Tom says, "History is when people and animals and places do something important or interesting. Like this picture. It shows a big dinosaur. Dinosaurs were animals that lived before us. They were very big and loud and scary. But they are not here anymore. They are history."
Amy says, "Wow, dinosaurs are cool. I wish I could see one. What is this picture, Tom?"
Tom says, "This picture is a man and a woman. They are wearing funny clothes and hats. They are history too. They lived a long time ago, when there were no cars or phones or TVs. They had different names and rules and games. Their names were George and Martha. They were the first president and first lady of our country."
Amy says, "That is interesting, Tom. I like their names. George and Martha. They sound nice. Do you think they were happy?"
Tom says, "I think so, Amy. They look happy in the picture. They are smiling and holding hands. They must have been glad to have each other and to help our country. I am glad they are in our history book. They are good people to learn from."
Amy says, "Me too, Tom. I like history. It is fun to see and hear about different things. Maybe we can find more history books and learn more. Can we keep this book, Tom?"
Tom says, "I don't know, Amy. Maybe we should ask someone. Maybe this book belongs to someone else. Maybe they left it here by mistake. We should be nice and try to find them. Maybe they will let us borrow it or give it to us. Or maybe they will tell us more stories about history."
Amy says, "OK, Tom. Let's do that. Let's look for the owner of the book. Maybe they are in the park too. Maybe they are our new friends. Come on, Tom, let's go."
Tom and Amy put the book back on the bench and run around the park, looking for the owner. They are happy and excited. They love history and they love each other. They are good friends.

Sara liked to help her mom with the laundry. She felt useful when she put the dirty clothes in the big basket and carried them to the machine. But sometimes the basket was too heavy for her, and she had to crawl on the floor with it.
One day, she was crawling with the basket to the machine, when she saw her brother Max playing with his toy cars. He had made a road with his blocks and was zooming his cars along it. Sara wanted to play with him, but she also wanted to help her mom.
"Max, can you help me with the laundry?" she asked.
"No, I'm busy. Go away," Max said.
"But it's too heavy for me. Please, Max," Sara said.
"I don't care. It's your job, not mine. Leave me alone," Max said.
Sara felt sad and angry. She didn't think it was fair that Max didn't help her. She thought of a way to make him help her. She crawled to the machine and put the basket on top of it. Then she crawled back to Max's road and knocked down his blocks with her feet.
"Hey, what are you doing?" Max shouted.
"I'm playing with your cars. They are fun," Sara said.
"No, they are mine. Stop it. You're ruining my road," Max said.
"Then help me with the laundry. It's our job, not mine," Sara said.
Max looked at his messed up road and his cars. He looked at the basket on the machine and Sara. He realized that he had been mean to her. He felt sorry and ashamed.
"Okay, okay. I'm sorry, Sara. I'll help you with the laundry. Come on, let's go," he said.
He took some clothes from the basket and crawled with Sara to the machine. They put the clothes in the machine and pushed the button. Then they crawled back to the road and fixed the blocks. They played with the cars together and had fun.
Sara smiled and hugged Max. She was happy that he helped her and played with her. She felt useful and loved.
